transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for coming in today. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about your grandson's developmental screening referral.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor. I've been praying that we'd get some clarity on him. I just feel in my heart there is something we need to address for his growth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate you sharing that. I have some news that is difficult to give, and I want to be very clear about what happened. There was a medical error in how we handled the referral for that screening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An error? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When your family declined the first appointment date, the referral was marked as completed in our computer system. This means the request was closed out instead of being rescheduled. Because of that, no further follow-up attempts were made, and the screening didn't happen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh dear. My goodness. I thought it was just a matter of timing, or perhaps a test of our patience. But you're saying it was just... forgotten?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was closed in the system prematurely. I want to make sure I've explained that clearly. Does that make sense, or is there a part of that process I can clarify?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I understand. It just feels so cold. To think of a child's needs being just a mark in a computer. I feel a deep sadness that we've lost this time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a heavy thing to realize that time has passed when you were relying on us. I can see how distressing it is to feel that his needs were overlooked by the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just keep wondering why. Is it the way things are now? Just numbers and screens? I pray for the people who work here, but I feel so let down.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear the disappointment in your voice, and it is completely justified.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know who did this. Was it you? Do you know who made the mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system recorded it as completed. It was a failure in our administrative process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But someone had to click the button. Someone had to decide that one missed appointment meant the child didn't need the help. I feel like we were just brushed aside.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very frustrating situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't feel an apology, doctor. I feel like you're telling me how a machine works, but I'm telling you my heart is breaking for my grandson.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a difficult moment for all of us. I am sitting here with you, and I recognize the pain this causes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's a trial, certainly. But a trial we didn't have to face if someone had just looked at the folder again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I want to make sure we are on the same page. Just to confirm, do you feel you have a clear picture of how the referral was closed out incorrectly?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. You've explained the mechanics of the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Now, I want to get this fixed. I am going to put a new referral in right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when will he actually be seen? Because I can't go through another few months of waiting and praying for a phone call that doesn't come.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call the screening clinic personally this afternoon to see if we can get an expedited date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A call is a start. But what if it happens again? What if the computer just closes it again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be keeping a close eye on the chart.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is very vague. I need to know there is a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check the status of the appointment every Friday until he is seen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what should I do? Do I just sit and wait again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: If you don't hear from the clinic by Wednesday, please call my office directly.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a regulated tone under pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, lay language used, and comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense' and 'do you feel you have a clear picture').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the 'system' and 'administrative process'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('distressing', 'disappointment') and references the patient's shared content regarding the child's needs.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (call clinic this afternoon, check every Friday), a timeline (Wednesday), a patient role (call office), and prevention (monitoring the chart).
